49708-the-garden-of-eden-stories-from-th.title: Of The Old Testament
49708-the-garden-of-eden-stories-from-th.creator: Unknown
49708-the-garden-of-eden-stories-from-th.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. This is the oldest story in the world. It began to be told when children began to ask questions; and that was very long ago. The children said, “Where did everything come from? Who made the hills and the sea? Who made the sun and the stars?” And their fathers and mothers answered as best they could.

The scene which a London fire presents can never be forgotten: the shouts of the crowd as it opens to let the engines dart through it, the foaming head of water springing out of the ground, and spreading over the road until it becomes a broad mirror reflecting the glowing blaze--the black, snake-like coils of the leather hose rising and falling like things of life, whilst a hundred arms work at the pump, their central heart--the applause that rings out clear above the roaring

arxiv-2109-00618.title: Rank of matrices with entries from a multiplicative group
arxiv-2109-00618.creator: Noga Alon, József Solymosi
arxiv-2109-00618.description: Abstract We establish lower bounds on the rank of matrices in which all but the diagonal entries lie in a multiplicative group of small rank. Applying these bounds we show that the distance sets of finite pointsets in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} generate high rank multiplicative groups and that multiplicative groups of small rank cannot contain large sumsets.

arxiv-2110-10998.title: Bayesian inference of ion velocity distribution function from laser-induced fluorescence spectra
arxiv-2110-10998.creator: S. Tokuda, Y. Kawachi, M. Sasaki, H. Arakawa, K. Yamasaki, K. Terasaka, S. Inagaki
arxiv-2110-10998.description: Abstract The velocity distribution function is a statistical description that connects particle kinetics and macroscopic parameters in many-body systems. Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) spectroscopy is utilized to measure the local velocity distribution function in spatially inhomogeneous plasmas. However, the analytic form of such a function for the system of interest is not always clear under the intricate factors in non-equilibrium states.

arxiv-2207-03319.title: Topological Speed Limit
arxiv-2207-03319.creator: Tan Van Vu, Keiji Saito
arxiv-2207-03319.description: Abstract Any physical system evolves at a finite speed that is constrained not only by the energetic cost but also by the topological structure of the underlying dynamics. In this Letter, by considering such structural information, we derive a unified topological speed limit for the evolution of physical states using an optimal transport approach.

arxiv-2301-10121.title: Generalized Object Search
arxiv-2301-10121.creator: Kaiyu Zheng
arxiv-2301-10121.description: Abstract Abstract of ”Generalized Object Search” by Kaiyu Zheng, Ph.D., Brown University, February, 2023 Future collaborative robots must be capable of finding objects. As such a fundamental skill, we expect object search to eventually become an off-the-shelf capability for any robot, similar to e.g. , object detection, SLAM, and motion planning. However, existing approaches either make unrealistic compromises ( e.g.

arxiv-2304-12799.title: TOWARDS A GENERALIZABLE SIMULATION FRAMEWORK TO STUDY COLLISIONS BETWEEN SPACECRAFT AND DEBRIS
arxiv-2304-12799.creator: Simone Asci, Angadh Nanjangud
arxiv-2304-12799.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Simone Asci, Angadh Nanjangud. In recent years, computer simulators of rigid-body systems have been successfully used to improve and expand the field of developing new space robots, becoming a leading tool for the preliminary investigation and evaluation of space robotic missions. However, the impressive progress in performance has not been matched yet by an improvement in modelling capabilities, which remain limited to very basic representations of real systems.

arxiv-2407-19736.title: Sensor Selection via GFlowNets: A Deep Generative Modeling Framework to Navigate Combinatorial Complexity
arxiv-2407-19736.creator: Spilios Evmorfos, Zhaoyi Xu, and Athina Petropulu
arxiv-2407-19736.description: Abstract The performance of sensor arrays in sensing and wireless communications improves with more elements, but this comes at the cost of increased energy consumption and hardware expense. This work addresses the challenge of selecting k k sensor elements from a set of m m to optimize a generic Quality-of-Service metric.

arxiv-2409-19587.title: Efficient Quality Control of Whole Slide Pathology Images with Human-in-the-loop Training
arxiv-2409-19587.creator: Abhijeet Patil, Harsh Diwakar, Jay Sawant, Nikhil Cherian Kurian
arxiv-2409-19587.description: Abstract Histopathology whole slide images (WSIs) are being widely used to develop deep learning-based diagnostic solutions, especially for precision oncology. Most of these diagnostic softwares are vulnerable to biases and impurities in the training and test data which can lead to inaccurate diagnoses.

arxiv-2601-06347.title: What Matters When Building Universal Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Models?
arxiv-2601-06347.creator: Jonas Golde Patrick Haller Alan Akbik
arxiv-2601-06347.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jonas Golde Patrick Haller Alan Akbik. Recent progress in universal multilingual named entity recognition (NER) has been driven by advances in multilingual transformer models and task-specific architectures, loss functions, and training datasets. Despite substantial prior work, we find that many critical design decisions for such models are made without systematic justification, with architectural components, training objectives, and data sources evaluated only in combination rather than in isolation.

bradley-appearance-reality-1893.title: Appearance and Reality
bradley-appearance-reality-1893.creator: F. H. Bradley
bradley-appearance-reality-1893.description: British idealism's summit; the monist metaphysics Moore and Russell rebelled against. Internet Archive edition.

pmc-11486503.title: MSDAFL: molecular substructure-based dual attention feature learning framework for predicting drug–drug interactions
pmc-11486503.creator: Chao Hou, Guihua Duan, Cheng Yan
pmc-11486503.description: MotivationDrug–drug interactions (DDIs) can cause unexpected adverse drug reactions, affecting treatment efficacy and patient safety. The need for computational methods to predict DDIs has been growing due to the necessity of identifying potential risks associated with drug combinations in advance.

pmc-11646897.title: ST-Segment Elevation
pmc-11646897.creator: Maria Cristina Carella, Cinzia Forleo, Marco Maria Dicorato, Alessio Falagario, Paolo Basile, Eugenio Carulli, Francesco Loizzi, Marco Matteo Ciccone, Andrea Igoren Guaricci
pmc-11646897.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A wide range of etiologies, both ischemic and nonischemic, can produce an electrocardiographic pattern of ST-segment elevation (STE), including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) and electrolyte imbalances. Instances of hypocalcemia-induced TTS and STE are exceedingly rare in medical literature. This paper presents the case of a 75-year-old woman with advanced ovarian cancer and no prior heart issues, who exhibited diffuse STE on electrocardiogram, resembling acute coronary syndrome.

pmc-12522699.title: Community-based strategies for tuberculosis control in migrant communities: how to integrate determinants of vulnerability into decision-making
pmc-12522699.creator: Helena Martínez Alguacil, Jordi Gómez i Prat, Valeria Pérez-Muto, Gabriela Tejada Panduro, Hakima Ouaarab Essadek, Alícia Garcia Circuns, Elisabet Sicart Torres, Mar López Espinilla, Jacobo Mendioroz Peña, Laura Gavaldà Mestre
pmc-12522699.description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge, particularly among migrant populations, who face increased vulnerability due to social and structural determinants of health. In Catalonia, Spain, the Model of Community and Public Action (MACIP) programme was launched in 2023 to improve TB prevention and care through culturally adapted, community-based interventions delivered by community health workers (CHWs).

pmc-12829019.title: A retail audit of mosquito control products in Bidibidi refugee settlement, northwestern Uganda
pmc-12829019.creator: Kaci D McCoy, Esther Nakyaze, Samantha W Tsang, Amy A Ellis, Mary Grace Alwano, Olive D’Mello, Suzanne Van Hulle, Steve A Harvey, Danielle Piccinini Black, Jarvice Sekajja
pmc-12829019.description: BackgroundUganda remains one of the highest malaria burden countries globally, with refugee populations disproportionately affected. While government-led initiatives, such as free distribution of insecticide-treatesd nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying, are key to the vector control response, limited data exist on the role of retail markets in providing complementary mosquito control products (MCPs) in refugee settings.

pmc-13191263.title: Modular design for drug delivery across hierarchical gastrointestinal barriers: From materials to systems
pmc-13191263.creator: Yaxin Chen, Qingyun Yang, Jian Yang, Jiquan Zhang
pmc-13191263.description: Drug delivery to the gastrointestinal (GI) tract necessitates overcoming multi-level physiological barriers from organ to cellular levels, which exhibit significant heterogeneity under pathological conditions. Conventional delivery strategies, constrained by single-function capabilities, struggle to achieve cross-scale coordination, severely limiting therapeutic efficacy.

pmc-13253259.title: Clinical characteristics of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in non-HIV patients: a retrospective study
pmc-13253259.creator: Mengyuan Li, Junsu Pan, Shuting Ye, Chongyang Wang, Jianhua Luo, Cheng Zheng
pmc-13253259.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the clinical characteristics and identify risk factors for severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) -negative patients.MethodsThis retrospective study included 39 non-HIV PJP patients diagnosed by next-generation sequencing (NGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) at Taizhou Municipal Hospital between June 2019 and March 2025.

pmc-13294395.title: Multifunctional nanotherapeutics for tumor microenvironment modulation in solid tumor therapy
pmc-13294395.creator: Mengqi Yang, Yedong Huang, Weiye Qian, Junye Zhu, Liu Fei, Zhixin Jiao, Jian Wang, Yifan Wang, Wenbo Zhu, Shun Chen, Peipei Gong, Ziheng Wang, Zhichao Lu, Rujun Liu, Zhining Liu, Qiaojun Hong, Qingyu Luo, Lin Zhang

pmc-13365024.title: Bloodstream infections and Blood-Brain barrier Permeability: An observational cohort study
pmc-13365024.creator: Jonathan Underwood, Kate Davies, Sam Loveless, Mara Cercignani, Nicholas G Dowell, Eva Periche-Tomas, Itamar Ronen, John Evans, James E McLaren, Neil A Harrison
pmc-13365024.description: Highlights•Bloodstream infection provides a novel model of severe systemic inflammation.•Bloodstream infection causes acute, inflammation-associated deficits in attention.•Elevations in biomarkers of brain injury correlate with severity of illness.•At convalescence cognition normalised, but depressive symptoms persisted.•No evidence of persistent blood–brain barrier dysfunction or microglial activation.

pmc-13437404.title: Neuromuscular training for preventing ankle joint injuries in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13437404.creator: Hexuan Xiang, Kexiang Yang, Huiling Liao, Xiaolong Zhang, Yunong Zhang, Hyun-Chul Jeong
pmc-13437404.description: Ankle joint injuries are among the most common sports-related injuries. However, determining the most effective training method to prevent these injuries remains a challenge. Neuromuscular training (NMT) is a preventive strategy aimed at reducing muscle and ligament injuries, yet its effectiveness in preventing ankle joint injuries is not fully understood, and robust clinical evidence is lacking.

pmc-13468417.title: Development and Optimization of Sodium Deoxycholate-Stabilised Shellac-Based Polymeric Nanoparticles for Enhanced Pharmacokinetics and Anticancer Activity of Etodolac in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
pmc-13468417.creator: Ritesh A. Fule, Aishwarya S. Rangurwar, Pankaj D. Nagpure, Helal G. Alanazi, Mohammed M. Alruwaili, Md Ali Mujtaba, Gamal Osman Elhassan, Siham Abdoun

pmc-13474885.title: Payment mechanism and medical quality: new evidence from China healthcare reform
pmc-13474885.creator: Yaxuan Zuo, Yingtan Mu, Jiali Zhang, Qiuming Hu
pmc-13474885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundReform of payment methods promote to achieve the public value of health insurance through incentive-compatible mechanisms. Payment differentials, defined as the difference between DRG/DIP payment amounts and total medical expenses, together with the rational design of surplus retention mechanisms, are crucial for controlling healthcare costs, improving service quality, ensuring the sustainability of health insurance funds, and guiding medical institutions towards reasonable surplus targets.MethodsThis study constructs a one-shot game model under conditions of information asymmetry among hospitals, patients, and health insurance agencies.

pmc-13565116.title: Prolonged In Vitro Expansion Shapes the Neuro-Supportive Potential of Jaw Periosteum Secretomes: Implications for Secretome Product Quality
pmc-13565116.creator: Yuling Wang, Nuo Chen, Felix Umrath, Marina Danalache, Andreas Naros, Julia C. Fitzgerald, Dorothea Alexander
pmc-13565116.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Prolonged in vitro expansion alters the composition and biological activity of JPC-derived secretomes, resulting in reduced neuro-supportive capacity.Proteomic profiling demonstrates a remodeling of the JPC secretome, characterized by a shift from regenerative, extracellular matrix-related factors toward inflammatory and stress-associated signaling.

pmc-13615507.title: GenART: Reading the genome’s language with adaptive “words”
pmc-13615507.creator: Kehan Chen, Ping Han, Zhe Lin, Shang Gao, Xinyu Yang, Xiangxiang Zeng, Yeyun Gong, Zhiliang Ji, Chen Lin
pmc-13615507.description: SummaryTokenization is both a prerequisite and a central challenge for genomic language models, due to the inherent difficulty of delineating meaningful segments within continuous DNA sequences. We present GenART, a genomic language model framework that dynamically segments DNA into variable-length words directly from raw sequences without manual annotation.
